q: Which of the following is identified as a reason for the Conservative government's decision to set up the Simon Commission ahead of schedule?
o: Pressure from the Muslim League
Fear of electoral defeat by the Labour Party, and a wish to avoid leaving India's constitutional future in 'irresponsible Labour hands'
Recommendations of the Nehru Report
A direct request from the Indian National Congress

q: The primary reason for the near-unanimous Indian anger against the Simon Commission was:
o: The complete exclusion of Indians from its membership, seen as a violation of the principle of self-determination
Its stance on separate electorates
Its recommendation for full dominion status
Its proposal for linguistic provinces

q: Regarding the Muslim League's response to the Simon Commission, which of the following is correct?
o: The League split, with Jinnah's faction at Calcutta opposing the commission while Muhammad Shafi's Lahore faction supported the government
The entire League unanimously supported the commission
The entire League unanimously boycotted the commission
The League refused to take any position on the issue

q: When the Simon Commission landed in Bombay on February 3, 1928, the Indian response included:
o: Complete public indifference to its arrival
Official welcome ceremonies organised by the Congress
Immediate cooperation from all political parties
A countrywide hartal, mass rallies, black flag demonstrations and slogans of 'Simon Go Back'

q: Dr Ambedkar, appointed by the Bombay Legislative Council to engage with the Simon Commission, argued before it (October 1928) for:
o: Separate electorates for all minorities without exception
Universal adult franchise for both men and women, provincial autonomy, and dyarchy at the Centre
Complete abolition of the Central Legislative Assembly
Immediate dominion status with no further negotiation

q: The Simon Commission's report did grant reserved seats to the depressed classes, but attached which condition that displeased Ambedkar?
o: Candidates had to have their competence endorsed by the provincial governor before contesting
Reserved seats would apply only in provinces where Muslims were also a minority
No woman could contest from a reserved seat
Depressed class candidates needed to secure Congress party endorsement

q: The Simon Commission published its final two-volume report in:
o: May 1930

q: Which of the following was a recommendation of the Simon Commission's report?
o: Introduction of universal adult franchise across India
Abolition of separate communal electorates entirely
Immediate grant of full dominion status to India
Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces, granting them autonomy, while rejecting parliamentary responsibility at the centre

q: Regarding communal electorates, the Simon Commission recommended that separate electorates be:
o: Retained permanently with no review
Abolished immediately and replaced with joint electorates
Retained (and even extended to other communities) until Hindu-Muslim tensions subsided
Replaced by proportional representation for all communities

q: The Nehru Report's recommendations were unanimous except on one key point, where the majority favoured 'dominion status' while a section (including younger leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru) wanted:
o: A unitary rather than federal structure
Complete independence as the constitutional basis
Continuation of dyarchy
Retention of separate electorates

q: Regarding electoral representation, the Nehru Report proposed:
o: Universal adult suffrage with no reservations of any kind
Joint electorates with reservation of seats for Muslims only in provinces where they were a minority
Reserved seats for Muslims even in Muslim-majority provinces like Punjab and Bengal
Separate electorates for all religious communities

q: The Nehru Report proposed a bicameral central legislature with which composition?
o: A 500-member House of Representatives elected by adult suffrage and a 200-member Senate elected by provincial councils
A Senate elected directly and a House nominated by the Governor-General
A 250-member unicameral legislature elected by limited franchise
A 1000-member House with no Senate

q: Which of the following was among the 19 fundamental rights proposed in the Nehru Report?
o: Right to maintain separate religious courts
Equal rights for women, right to form unions, and universal adult suffrage
Right to secede from the Indian union
Right to private property without any restriction

q: The Hindu Mahasabha's opposition to the Delhi Proposals and later the League's demands centred on its rejection of:
o: Any form of joint electorates
Dominion status as a constitutional goal
The concept of fundamental rights in the constitution
New Muslim-majority provinces and Muslim seat reservations in Punjab/Bengal that would ensure Muslim control of those legislatures

q: At the All Parties Conference in Calcutta (December 1928), Jinnah proposed three amendments to the Nehru Report, including:
o: Abolition of the Senate in the proposed bicameral legislature
One-third Muslim representation in the central legislature, proportional reservation in Bengal/Punjab till adult suffrage, and residual powers to provinces
Introduction of a unitary constitutional structure
Complete rejection of dominion status in favour of immediate independence

q: Jinnah's Fourteen Points included a demand that no bill or resolution in any legislature be passed if what proportion of a minority community considered it against their interests?
o: One-half
One-third
Two-thirds
Three-fourths

q: Which of the following best summarises the overall political impact of the Simon Commission's appointment on the Indian national movement?
o: It gave a stimulus to radical forces demanding complete independence and socio-economic reform, while also spurring the first Indian attempt at drafting a constitution
It had no effect on Indian political mobilisation whatsoever
It ended all communal tensions in Indian politics permanently
It led to immediate and full self-government being granted to India
